scenarios.title: FORMAT EXAMPLE — replace with an original situation
scenarios.objective: Locate the defender relative to a passing lane.
scenarios.briefing: YOU have the puck. Teammate 1 and gold F1 are both visible. Compare their positions.
cues: YOU have the puck. Teammate 1 and gold F1 are both visible. Compare their positions.
scenarios.limits: Static practice scene. Any earlier action or hypothetical change is stated in words; speed and outcomes are not simulated.

sources.title: Hockey Canada: Vision and Scanning
sources.use: Scanning and reassessment theme; does not certify this scene or key.

questions.prompt: Is F1 between YOU and teammate 1 in this freeze?

options.text: No, F1 is away from that passing lane
Yes, F1 is on that passing lane

questions.explanation: F1 is away from the straight lane joining YOU and 1. This describes the current picture; it does not mean a pass is always better than keeping the puck.

questions.prompt: Suppose F1 moves into the lane to teammate 1. What would you check before passing?
questions.explanation: Check whether another lane is open and whether you have space to keep the puck. If the lane to 1 has closed, you can delay or choose another option. Explain which cue would guide your choice.

questions.prompt: Which two statements match the current positions?

options.text: Teammate 1 is farther toward the right-hand net than F1
F1 is on the straight passing lane to 1

questions.explanation: Teammate 1 is farther toward the right-hand net on the overhead board, and YOU have the puck. F1 is offset from the direct passing lane.

questions.prompt: Put this scan-and-decide routine in a useful order for the current freeze.

options.text: Locate F1 and the lane to teammate 1
Check another support lane or space
Choose whether to pass, carry, or keep the puck

questions.explanation: This is one suggested scan-to-decision routine: see the pressure, check support, then choose an action. Players may scan in a slightly different order when the picture changes; the routine is not the only possible temporal action.

questions.prompt: Place teammate 1 in a support position that opens a different passing angle from YOU.
questions.explanation: A support spot with separation can give the puck carrier another angle. This is a coaching suggestion to discuss, not an objectively graded single correct location.

questions.prompt: Suppose 1 moves behind F1 along the same passing line from YOU. What is a useful next step?

options.text: Use the same straight lane to 1

questions.explanation: In that hypothetical, the receiver has moved behind the defender on the passing line. Check for a new lane or keep the puck while another option develops.
